scope: Changed-boundary preflight for shared-interface repair; no model calls or scientific outcome assessment
checks: Research requests, tasks, scientific arm policies, API loop and evaluator are byte-identical to the predecessor. Fresh authors receive no old source cache, generator, numerical result or reference answer.

Both arms receive the same revised mechanical contract. model_spec is stored directly and passed as the same JSON object to the unchanged worker; it is neither wrapped nor automatically unwrapped, including author-chosen task/model keys.
Unchanged gateway screens full returned records before the compact projection. Screening exclusions, source acquisition, available full texts, hit order and scientific access are unchanged.

Compact cards preserve complete identity fields or explicitly flag oversized-identity stubs with recoverable identity pages. Abstract previews carry completeness and full-length labels; complete abstracts and original records remain available.

Stable search/hit IDs and canonical record hashes bind recoverable data. Cached record/abstract/identity pages verify the original cache hash and use no new HTTP requests. Provider cursor and cached-record cursor have distinct semantics.
Provider total/retrieved/rejected counts are retained separately from current cached accepted count. No source is silently dropped, reranked or summarized by scientific content.
All prior credential, request reservation, full Responses history, isolation, no-duplicate dispatch, explicit final selection and all-four-episode closure boundaries are inherited unchanged.

Same per-episode USD4, 24 calls, 250000 input bytes, retrieval/trial limits and statistical operators remain. New batch USD15 global ceiling plus old actual USD0.8666782 stays within USD16; global cap change is explicit.

Diagnostic/final seeds are reused as declared. All12 final slots remain required. A fresh-constructor rerun does not estimate a paired causal interface effect or create independent clinical validation.
Postrun audit adapter counts actually returned cards and requested cached-hit pages, and treats the complete submitted model_spec as author-owned rather than assuming a host wrapper.
